title: Add a Windows CI job and Windows install docs
lead:
Fourth child of s13. Proves the unit suite on a real Windows runner and
documents installation.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The children before this one verify their Windows branches by patching
`os.name`. Only a real Windows run catches what patching cannot, such as path
separators, CRLF and file locking. Without docs, Windows users cannot get Pango,
GTK and Pandoc in place.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
.github/workflows/test.yml, test_quire.py and test_render.py (only POSIX-only
fixtures such as `#!/bin/sh` fakes, which get skipped or made portable),
README.md, AGENTS.md (the Windows note under Behavior to preserve), CHANGELOG.md.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Add a `windows-latest` job running `python test_quire.py` with Python 3.11 or
  newer and `shell: bash`. It must go green.
- Tests that need POSIX semantics carry a
  `skipIf(os.name == "nt", reason)` that states why. No test is skipped on
  POSIX.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
- Add the CI job, matching the existing fetch steps.
- Make each failing fixture portable, or skip it with a reason.
- Add a README section for Windows: Pandoc via its MSI or winget, the GTK and
  Pango runtime via MSYS2 as WeasyPrint's docs describe, then
  `py install.py`, the `.cmd` launchers in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\quire`, and
  adding that directory to PATH.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: python3 test_quire.py; black --check quire.py test_quire.py; flake8 quire.py test_quire.py; the windows-latest CI job is green.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Do not commit; orchestrator handles it.
